title: Obesity in Adults: Primary Care Weight Management Pathway

evidenceAudit.scope: Respectful adult primary-care identification, assessment and behavioural weight-management referral using NICE NG246.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national adult obesity pathway was opened.
Pharmacotherapy and bariatric-surgery criteria are outside this topic.
SFDA status is not applicable because no drug is prescribed.

pathophysiology.summary: Sustained positive energy balance increases adipose tissue mass. Visceral adiposity contributes to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk. Sleep, medicines, mental health and social context can affect weight and treatment access. Stigma and diagnostic overshadowing can delay care for unrelated symptoms.
keyMechanisms: Sustained positive energy balance increases adipose tissue mass.
Visceral adiposity contributes to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk.
Sleep, medicines, mental health and social context can affect weight and treatment access.

references.title: NICE NG246: Overweight and obesity management

symptoms: Weight-related mobility limitation, breathlessness, sleep symptoms or psychosocial distress; many adults are asymptomatic.
physicalSigns: Raised BMI, increased waist-to-height ratio or obesity-associated comorbidity.
redFlags: Symptoms suggesting an alternative urgent diagnosis, severe eating disorder, acute mental-health risk or suspected endocrine cause with rapid unexplained change.
precipitants: Energy-dense diet, low activity, sleep disruption, weight-promoting medicines, mental-health factors and social barriers.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Rapid change or characteristic endocrine, medication or fluid-retention features rather than gradual adiposity.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Classify using the current NICE adult BMI table and interpret alongside central adiposity
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports shared discussion and service selection; do not use alone to diagnose every risk.
ruleIn.normalValue: 18.5–24.9 kg/m² is the conventional healthy range

references.title: NICE NG246: Overweight and obesity management

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Raised ratio indicates increasing central adiposity risk
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Measure waist when BMI is below 35 kg/m².
ruleIn.normalValue: Waist less than half of height is the public-health message

clinicalManagement.title: Open the discussion
actions: Address the presenting problem first; ask permission before discussing weight or taking measurements.
Use respectful, non-judgemental language and ask what matters to the person.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess health and context
actions: Record height, weight and central adiposity as appropriate; assess comorbidities, medicines, sleep, mental wellbeing and barriers.
Agree achievable health and weight goals rather than imposing a target.

clinicalManagement.title: Offer multicomponent support
actions: Offer or refer to a programme combining dietary energy deficit, physical activity and behaviour-change support.
Track agreed goals and weight during the programme, then plan maintenance and relapse support.

medicationPlan.note: This primary-care topic covers behavioural and service pathways. Weight-management medicines require a separate eligibility, contraindication and monitoring pathway.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: With permission, record height, weight and waist circumference when BMI is below 35 kg/m² so waist-to-height ratio can be calculated.

teaching.scope: Respectful adult primary-care identification, assessment and behavioural weight-management referral using NICE NG246.
learningObjectives: Discuss weight with permission and without stigma.
Select a multicomponent intervention around individual needs.
pitfalls: Offering a restrictive diet without trained support or maintenance planning.
keyPoints: Treat unrelated symptoms on their own merits.
Central adiposity adds risk information when BMI is below 35 kg/m².

references.title: NICE NG246: Overweight and obesity management

patientEducation: Explain BMI and waist measures as risk tools, not personal judgements.
lifestyleAndDiet: Agree a sustainable energy deficit, activity plan, sleep support and behaviour-change goals.
mdtReferrals: Dietitian or registered nutrition professional, exercise service, psychology and specialist obesity service when indicated.
dischargeCriteria: Goals and maintenance plan agreed, comorbidities addressed and the person knows how to re-access support.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Monitor agreed goals during the programme and review maintenance at 1 year or sooner if health needs change.
